question.text:
Let D = diag(1, 1, −1, −1). What is the real dimension of the space of Hermitian 4 × 4 matrices
H satisfying DH + HD = 0?
(A) 6 (B) 8 (C) 16 (D) 4 (E) 10

solution.text:
In two-by-two block form, the equation forces both diagonal blocks of H to vanish. The
upper-right block is an arbitrary complex 2 × 2 matrix, and the lower-left block is its
conjugate transpose. Four complex parameters give eight real dimensions.

question.text:
For arbitrary Hermitian matrices H, K of the same size, which matrices must be Hermitian? I.
HK; II. HK + KH; III. i(HK − KH).
(A) I only (B) II only (C) I and II only (D) II and III only (E) I, II, and III

solution.text:
∗
Conjugate transpose reverses products, so (HK) = KH. Thus HK is Hermitian only if
∗
the factors commute. In contrast, (HK + KH) = HK + KH, and conjugating the scalar i
∗
supplies the minus sign that makes [i(HK − KH)] = i(HK − KH). Noncommuting Hermi-
tian matrices provide counterexamples to I.
